column1: # WINDOW-WAITS-UNREAD-RECEIVERS - the calls the bare-site inventory's reader cannot read (T-WINDOW-WAITS-READER-SEES-MATCH-BOUND-HANDLES,
# 0.4.10 plan row 19, rulings R4 and R6).
# One row per (crate, cfg arm, item, the vocabulary entries the call could be): a product call where the reader of
# vocabulary method's name and argument count (`METHOD_ARITIES`) on a receiver it gives no type, or one that is not one
# chain, or a `write!`/`writeln!` whose first argument has no type. Each may be a site the inventory does not count; the
# reading cannot say, so it is listed here instead of passed over. `entries` joins the candidates with " | "; `calls`
# counts them in the item. A call in a door function's body is listed too: it may be an effect its `# effects` row
# Held equal to the code by `hang_watch::window_waits_tests::every_unread_vocabulary_call_is_a_row_and_every_row_a_call`,
# which leaves the observed list, with these reasons, in target/WINDOW-WAITS-UNREAD-RECEIVERS.tsv; every reason is
# `YYYY-MM-DD: why`. `scripts/ci/check-window-waits.ps1` (check 8) refuses a row added, or grown past its count at the
# merge base, unless its reason is dated and is not a reason the merge base's list already gives. A row goes when its
# receiver is typed (the reading's grammar grows) or its call is gone. A2e's lint, which reads the compiler's types,
# ends the list with the inventory.
